Anderlecht.wav}}, {{IPA|de|ˈandɐlɛçt|lang}}) or '''RSCA''' ({{IPA|nl|ˌɛr.ɛs.seːˈaː, -ˈʔaː|lang}}, {{IPA|fr|ɛʁ.ɛs.se.ɑ|lang|RSCA FR.wav}}, {{IPA|de|ˌɛʁʔɛs.tseːˈʔaː|lang}}) is a Belgian professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Anderlecht]], [[Brussels]] Capital-Region. Anderlecht plays in the [[Belgian Pro League]] and is the most successful Belgian football team in European competitions, with five trophies, as well as in the Belgian domestic league, with 34 championship wins. They have also won nine [[Belgian Cup]]s and hold the record for most consecutive Belgian championship titles, winning five between the [[1963–64 Belgian First Division|1963–64]] and [[1967–68 Belgian First Division|1967–68]] seasons. Founded in 1908, the club first reached the highest level in Belgian football in [[1921–22 Belgian First Division|1921–22]] and have been playing in the first division continuously since [[1935–36 Belgian First Division|1935–36]]. They won their first major trophy after [[World War II]] with a championship win in [[1946–47 Belgian First Division|1946–47]]. They never finished outside the top six of the Belgian first division with the exception of [[2019–20 Belgian First Division A|2019–20]] (8th) and [[2022–23 Belgian Pro League|2022–23]] (11th). They are ranked 14th amongst all-time [[List of UEFA club competition winners|UEFA club competition winners]], tenth in the [[International Federation of Football History & Statistics]] continental Clubs of the 20th Century European ranking and were 41st in the 2012 [[UEFA ranking|UEFA team rankings]].{{cite web |url=http://kassiesa.home.xs4all.nl/bert/uefa/data/method4/trank2012.html |title=UEFA coefficient |access-date=28 August 2012 |archive-date=4 March 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130304090741/http://kassiesa.home.xs4all.nl/bert/uefa/data/method4/trank2012.html |url-status=dead }} In 1986, they achieved their best UEFA ranking with a joint first place with [[Juventus FC|Juventus]].{{cite web |url=http://www.xs4all.nl/~kassiesa/bert/uefa/data/method1/trank1986.html |title=UEFA coefficient |access-date=1 November 2010 |archive-date=27 October 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091027005502/http://www.xs4all.nl/~kassiesa/bert/uefa/data/method1/trank1986.html |url-status=live }} Anderlecht have been playing their matches in the [[Astrid Park]] in the municipality of Anderlecht since 1917. Their current stadium was renamed Lotto Park in 2019. Previously it was called [[Constant Vanden Stock Stadium]] which was first opened in 1983 to replace the former Emile Versé Stadium. They play in purple and white outfits. They have long-standing rivalries with [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] and [[Standard Liège]]."}}
